note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Acute viral upper respiratory illness with dry cough, runny nose, sore throat, fatigue, and mild shortness of breath; plan emphasizes supportive care with a short course of antibiotics only if no improvement.

History:
- Presenting complaint: Several days of feeling unwell with cough/cold symptoms and fatigue; reported shortness of breath on occasion.
- Time line: Symptoms started approximately 4–5 days ago (around Saturday); currently persistent but not improving; associated feverish sensations and night sweats noted.
- Cough: Mostly dry, with occasional production; worse in the morning.
- Nasal symptoms: Runny nose.
- Throat/Ears: Sore throat; occasional ear fullness.
- Breathing: Shortness of breath reported, but no chest pain; no wheeze documented.
- Fever/rigors: Intermittent hot/cold sensations with night sweats.
- GI: Diarrhea on day 1 of illness; subsequently resolved.
- Appetite: Appetite reported as adequate; fluid intake encouraged.
- Exposures/initiating factors: Recent social outing (celebration) prior to onset; no clear dietary cause identified.
- Exacerbating/relieving factors: Hoarseness related to shouting at football; rest and fluids advised.
- Associated symptoms: Overall fatigue; mild muscle/joint stiffness.
- ROS (systems review): No chest pain; no significant edema or focal neurologic symptoms described.

Past Medical History:
- Diabetes mellitus type 2 (patient stated; there is a conflicting statement during history: “type two” then “type one”; conflict noted)
- Hypertension
- Overweight/obesity described by patient
- History of hearing decline (mew minor)
- No known drug allergies reported

Medications:
- Metformin (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Lisinopril (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Aspirin PRN (dose/route/frequency not documented)
- Amoxicillin (proposed antibiotic if no improvement; dose/route not documented; frequency stated as three times daily)

Social History:
- Living situation: Lives with wife; no children at home
- Occupation: Works in a factory manufacturing steel parts
- Smoking: Occasional smoker; actively cutting down
- Alcohol: Approximately 9 pints per week (primarily weekends)
- Vaping: Using a vaporizer as part of tobacco reduction
- Financial/lifestyle: Not specifically detailed beyond occupation and home life

Family History:
- Not documented

Physical Examination:
- Vitals: Not documented
- Exam findings: Not documented beyond patient-reported symptoms (sniffles but no formal findings recorded)

Investigations:
- None discussed or documented

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: Acute viral upper respiratory illness (likely viral/early flu)
  - Plan:
    - Supportive care: rest, increased fluids
    - Paracetamol for fever/discomfort (dose/route not documented)
    - No antibiotics at this time
    - Antibiotic prescription offered if no improvement within 24–48 hours:
      - Amoxicillin: 1 tablet three times daily; dose/route not documented
    - Follow-up: If not better by next week, return for re-evaluation

- Issue 2: Chronic conditions (diabetes mellitus type 2; hypertension)
  - Plan:
    - Continue current medications (Metformin and Lisinopril); no changes documented today
    - No acute changes to chronic disease management noted

- Issue 3: Supportive care and safety counseling
  - Plan:
    - Encourage rest and hydration
    - Monitor for worsening shortness of breath or new chest pain; return if symptoms worsen or fail to improve
    - Reassess in follow-up if symptoms persist beyond a week

General Plan:
- Provide symptomatic relief and monitor for progression to bacterial infection; initiate antibiotics only if symptoms persist/worsen
- Encourage continuing current chronic medications
- Advise hydration, rest, and over-the-counter fever management as tolerated
